objects.title: HyperCities as an open, unrealized idea
objects.summary: Imagines a geotemporal way of finding lives, events, historical maps, documents, and futures without reducing HyperCities to a finished platform.

objects.title: Mapping as relational, ongoing practice
objects.summary: Defines maps as propositions and relations, and frames georeferencing as the keying of one representation to another rather than a correction toward reality.

provenance.locator: Opening of Thick Mapping through transition to Digital Humanities

objects.title: The flaneur as time-traveler
objects.summary: Reads Benjamin's flaneur as a figure who moves on a street while descending into vanished time, making care for muted pasts an interpretive practice.

provenance.locator: Opening pages; subsection Legibility / Recognizability begins on page 23

objects.title: Berlin's coexisting pasts
objects.summary: Describes Berlin as overlapping, uneven remains whose pasts coexist in the present rather than lining up as a single chronology.

provenance.locator: Berlin discussion leading to film and new media

objects.title: Ghost Maps as reading places
objects.summary: Presents historical interpretation as reading place, joining cartographic depictions with verbal narratives to make prior actions and their ghosts perceptible.

provenance.locator: Opening Window 1 through Ghost Map method

objects.title: Ghost map as thick, revisitable document
objects.summary: Defines ghost maps as dense composites of archival cartography and digital GIS that reveal time, change, events, and motion without being reducible to illustrations.

provenance.locator: Ghost map composition and Los Angeles layers

objects.title: Georeferencing as a relation among representations
objects.summary: Contrasts a normative basemap with infinite regress, then treats alignment as the production of a relation rather than the discovery of a final truth.

objects.title: Spatial deformance and alternative basemaps
objects.summary: Uses georectification experiments to make the politics of projections, positional choices, and competing spatial epistemologies available for examination.

provenance.locator: Omi and Ortelius experiments through Ideologies of Accuracy

objects.title: Ideologies of accuracy
objects.summary: Treats accuracy as purpose-bound and argues for strategic, critical use of dominant mapping platforms that preserves contestation and alternative histories.

objects.title: Participatory digital humanities
objects.summary: Frames participation as an aspiration to make cultural-record creation available across differences while remaining attentive to the conditions of access and power.

objects.title: Events, witnesses, and multiple temporalities
objects.summary: Develops HyperCities Now through the singular tweet, its historical and networked temporalities, and the ethical distance between observer and witness.

provenance.locator: On the Event: HyperCities Now (Egypt, Libya, Japan)

objects.title: Tohoku, social media, and scale
objects.summary: Moves between a plea for help, crisis volunteers, aggregate Twitter analysis, and individual stories after the 2011 earthquake and tsunami.

provenance.locator: The Role of Social Media through emotions charted over time

objects.title: Tohoku gallery: embodied witnessing
objects.summary: Shifts from distant analysis to visits in Tohoku and the Fukushima evacuation zone, ending with an ongoing obligation to witness for witnesses.

objects.text: HyperCities doesn’t exist. It’s an idea, largely unrealized, perhaps impossible.

objects.text: Mapping is not a one-time thing.
As the flâneur walked along the streets, he was conducted downward in time.
The historian who maps the past makes these ghosts visible.
It is turtles all the way down.
